blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — sequential compression device safety and VTE prevention after arthroplasty
stem: A client with a prior DVT is recovering after total hip arthroplasty. The client reports calf discomfort from the sequential compression device and asks to leave it off. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Remove the compression device for the rest of the shift and rely on the prescribed anticoagulant, without further calf assessment or review of the prophylaxis plan.
options.B: Leave the compression device off and keep the client in bed until the surgeon rounds, withholding ordered ambulation because calf discomfort makes mobility unsafe.
options.C: Pause the device, assess the calf and device fit, review the prescribed VTE-prevention plan, report the discomfort, and continue ordered mobilization if assessment supports safe activity.
options.D: Lower the compression pressure or change its schedule independently so the device is used intermittently, without contacting the care team about the discomfort.

rationale: A prior VTE places a joint-arthroplasty client at higher thromboembolic risk. Current AAOS discussion supports risk-stratified, multimodal prevention using chemoprophylaxis together with early mobilization and mechanical prophylaxis. Calf discomfort therefore warrants prompt assessment, review of device fit and the prescribed prevention plan, and escalation to the care team rather than unilateral discontinuation, bed rest, or independent device-setting changes. Therefore C is correct.
educational_objective: Respond to sequential-compression-device discomfort after arthroplasty by assessing and escalating the concern without independently abandoning prescribed VTE prophylaxis or ordered mobilization.
source_document_title: Aspirin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after hip and knee arthroplasty is not one-size-fits-all; AAOS Now commentary on risk-stratified VTE prevention
source_locator: AAOS Now 2026: prior thromboembolism identifies higher VTE risk; comprehensive prevention includes patient assessment, early mobilization, and mechanical prophylaxis in addition to risk-appropriate chemoprophylaxis.
source_claim_supported: Clients with prior VTE are higher risk after arthroplasty and should receive risk-stratified multimodal prophylaxis; discomfort with a compression device warrants assessment and care-team review rather than unilateral abandonment of prophylaxis or mobility.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential: apply and/or maintain devices used to promote venous return and use precautions to prevent postoperative complications.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed the only-based distractor cue and rewrote all options as complete device-management plans of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms C uniquely matches current AAOS risk-stratified VTE-prevention principles and safe nursing escalation; no residual absolute-word cue or second answer remains.
